page.content:
Imperial capital on the Bosporus, now Istanbul.

How Constantinople connects

  • Topic: Byzantine Empire — Constantinople was the imperial capital.
  • Character: Constantine the Great — Constantine founded Constantinople as New Rome.
  • Location: Hagia Sophia — Hagia Sophia stands in Constantinople.
  • Event: Fourth Crusade — The Fourth Crusade sacked Constantinople in 1204.
  • Location: Theodosian Walls — The Theodosian Walls guarded the city's land side.
  • Location: Hippodrome of Constantinople — The Hippodrome was the capital's public arena.
  • Location: Bosporus — The capital sits on the Bosporus.
  • Faction: Latin Empire — The Latin Empire occupied Constantinople.
  • Event: Recapture of Constantinople (1261) — Michael VIII recovered the capital in 1261.
  • Faction: Eastern Orthodox Church — The Ecumenical Patriarchate sat in Constantinople.
  • Weapon: Greek fire — Greek fire helped defend the capital's waters.
  • Faction: Varangian Guard — The Varangians guarded the emperor in the capital.

What is Constantinople?

Constantinople was Constantine the Great's New Rome: the walled capital on the Bosporus, seat of emperors, patriarchs, and the Hippodrome, until Mehmet II took the city in 1453.

Key threads lead to Byzantine Empire, Constantine the Great, Hagia Sophia, Fourth Crusade, Theodosian Walls and Hippodrome of Constantinople.
